hints: Focus on what ester hydrolysis always gives you, a carboxylic acid from the acyl part and an alcohol from the alkyl part.
Remember that a carboxylic acid can be reduced to a primary alcohol with the same carbon skeleton, so look for an acid and alcohol with matching carbons.
Split each ester into its acid plus alcohol and check which pair has the same branched chain where the alcohol is primary.
walkthrough:
**Recall ester hydrolysis**

Think of an ester as acid + alcohol joined together with water removed. Hydrolysis splits it back.

$$\text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Recall what reduction can do**

A carboxylic acid can be reduced to a primary alcohol with the same carbon skeleton.

$$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{[H]} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$
So we need the alcohol product to be primary and to have the same number of carbons and same skeleton as the acid part.

**Split option B and check**

For $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$, the acid part is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$ which is 2-methylpropanoic acid.

The alcohol part is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ which is 2-methylpropan-1-ol. Both are $\text{C}_4$ with the same branched skeleton, and the alcohol is primary.

**Confirm the reduction link**

Reduction of the acid gives exactly that primary alcohol.

$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH} \xrightarrow{[H]} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$$
So one hydrolysis product can be reduced to the other, which is what the question asks for.

options.A: Hydrolysis of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ gives propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ ($\text{C}_3$) and methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_1$). Different carbon counts mean reduction of the acid gives propan-1-ol, not methanol.
options.B: Hydrolysis gives 2-methylpropanoic acid, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$, and 2-methylpropan-1-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$. Both have 4 carbons with the same skeleton and the alcohol is primary, so reduction of the acid produces the alcohol.
options.C: Hydrolysis gives propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, and propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$. Although both are $\text{C}_3$, the alcohol is secondary. Reduction of a carboxylic acid gives a primary alcohol (propan-1-ol), never propan-2-ol.
options.D: Hydrolysis of $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCO}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ gives 2-methylpropanoic acid ($\text{C}_4$) and propan-2-ol ($\text{C}_3$). The carbon numbers differ and the alcohol is secondary, so the acid cannot be reduced to this alcohol.
